The probability of drawing at least one red ball is calculated as 1 minus the probability of drawing only blue balls. The probability of drawing only blue balls is (2/10) * (1/9) = 1/45. Therefore, the probability of drawing at least one red ball is 1 - 1/45 = 44/45. Now, we want to find the probability that both balls are red given that at least one ball is red. This is calculated using the conditional probability formula P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B). In this case, P(A and B) is the probability of drawing two red balls, which is (8/10) * (7/9) = 56/90. P(B) is the probability of drawing at least one red ball, which is 44/45. Therefore, the probability that both balls are red given that at least one ball is red is (56/90) / (44/45) = 14/22 = 7/11.
